clue.text: When is inlet only intermittently suitable to fish?

definitions.text: When is inlet only intermittently suitable to fish?

parts.words: When is inlet only intermittently suitable to fish?
parts.note: read as a riddle about the twice-monthly time when the sea rises least, so a shallow inlet holds little water for an angler

explanation.surface: An angler wonders when a creek offers only patchy fishing.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide with the smallest range, coming twice a lunar month, leaves inlets least flooded at high water.

clue.text: Crowned and beheaded

explanation.surface: A monarch is crowned and then executed, a short royal career.
explanation.definitionFit: To top something is to put a crown or cap on it, and also to cut off its head, as with a vegetable or a person.

clue.text: Model girl finally ditched tenor

indicators.note: the closing letter of the girl's word is dropped and something else takes its place

parts.note: lass is a northern word for a girl
T is the abbreviation for tenor in music

explanation.surface: A fashion model's boyfriend, a singer, is dumped at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally ditched' removes the last S of LASS and T for 'tenor' goes in its place. 'Model' is not a catwalk figure: it is the cobbler's wooden foot shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoemaker's last is a wooden form or pattern of a foot on which shoes are shaped.

clue.text: Six caught up in corded tangle separated

indicators.note: caught says one piece is held inside another
a tangle puts the letters of corded into a jumbled order
in a down clue, up means the numeral is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Six people get caught up in a knot of cords and are pulled apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tangle' makes DORCED, 'up' turns the numeral round to IV, and 'caught' sets it inside; 'in' is only a link, though it looks like the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A divorced couple are legally separated, their marriage dissolved.

clue.text: King Edward has taken sick and wasted

indicators.note: has taken means one piece now holds another within it

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
Ed is the short form of Edward
ill means sick

explanation.surface: King Edward falls ill and wastes away.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang 'wasted' means murdered or done away with, so slain.

clue.text: Restrictive order from initially amorous bullying ogre confining last of wives

indicators.note: confining says the opening letters hold something inside them
initially says take the first letter of each of the next three words
last of picks the closing letter of the word wives

explanation.surface: An amorous bully keeps his wives locked up and is served with a court order.
explanation.walkthrough: An ASBO is a British anti-social behaviour order, a court order restraining nuisance behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: An anti-social behaviour order is a British court order that restricts what someone may do.

clue.text: Woman sparing time for American girl

indicators.note: sparing means doing without, so a letter is left out

parts.note: Janet is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman makes time for an American girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link. In American slang a jane is any girl or woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane is US slang for a girl or woman, as in Plain Jane.

clue.text: Mantle nun abandoned in dissolution

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild, unrestrained, so the letters of the two words run free into a new order

explanation.surface: A nun throws off her mantle when her vows are dissolved.
explanation.definitionFit: An annulment declares a marriage void, the formal ending or undoing of it.

clue.text: Capote is upset about current obscurities

indicators.note: about means going round, so the scrambled letters surround another piece
upset knocks the letters of Capote is into another arrangement

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Truman Capote is irritated by today's murky writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' makes OPACTIES, and 'about' wraps those letters round I, the physics symbol for current.
explanation.definitionFit: Opacity is murkiness or unclearness, so the plural names instances of obscure, cloudy things.

clue.text: Grab a quick shot on horseback

parts.note: a snap is a quick photograph
a jockey who is up is riding, mounted on the horse

explanation.surface: A photographer grabs a fast picture while riding.
explanation.definitionFit: To snap up something is to seize it eagerly, as a bargain.

clue.text: Overly embracing most of masses in farewell

indicators.note: embracing means holding inside, so one piece is opened round another

parts.note: too means overly, excessively

indicators.note: most of drops the final letter of the word for masses

parts.note: oodles means masses, lots

explanation.surface: Someone says goodbye with excessive hugs all round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the final S, and 'embracing' splits the first piece after its T to take the trimmed word.
explanation.definitionFit: A jaunty, old-fashioned British way of saying goodbye or cheerio.

clue.text: Pleased I assembled a group of stars

indicators.note: assembled says the letters are put together into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted to have gathered a constellation of celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seven Sisters cluster in Taurus, a bright open cluster of stars.

clue.text: Paid for rose

explanation.surface: Someone stands a round, then gets to their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand someone a drink is to treat them to it; to stand is also to get up on one's feet.

clue.text: Green medic backing fishing dispute

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the whole run of two words is read in reverse

parts.note: raw means green, inexperienced
doc is short for doctor

explanation.surface: An inexperienced doctor supports one side in a fishing row.
explanation.walkthrough: The COD WARS were disputes between Britain and Iceland over fishing rights.
explanation.definitionFit: Series of clashes between Britain and Iceland over North Atlantic fishing grounds in the 1950s-70s.

clue.text: Spanish native, one in ancient Greek vessel seen at sea

indicators.note: in places one piece within another

parts.note: the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth
a means one

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the word seen is jumbled

explanation.surface: A Spaniard is spotted aboard an old Greek ship out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from Aragon, a region of north-east Spain.

clue.text: Entertain broadcast of certain death

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so we want a word that sounds like another

parts.note: fate is a person's destined end, death that cannot be escaped

explanation.surface: A radio report announces someone's inevitable death.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English the French-derived word for a festival is said 'fate'.
explanation.definitionFit: To fete someone is to honour them lavishly with celebration and hospitality.

clue.text: Diego worked out the shape of the earth

indicators.note: worked out suggests the letters of Diego are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Diego calculated the form of our planet.
explanation.definitionFit: A geoid is the model figure of the planet, its mean sea-level surface.

clue.text: Some younger man I consulted about a group of languages

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A man asks a younger colleague about language families.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'about' in the definition, but 'about a group of languages' cannot stand for the answer; 'about' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The family of tongues including English, German, Dutch and the Scandinavian ones.

clue.text: Feeble starters of watery egg and kippers

indicators.note: starters of says take the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A breakfast of runny egg and kippers is a poor start.
explanation.walkthrough: Kippers are smoked herrings, a traditional British breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: Weak and feeble both mean lacking strength.

clue.text: Quite rich source awaiting attention

parts.note: a well is a source of water
a job still to do is awaiting attention

explanation.surface: A rich source of income needs looking after.
explanation.definitionFit: Being comfortably off means wealthy, prosperous.

clue.text: Maybe she makes engravings and other things, that woman

parts.note: etc, et cetera, means and other things
her refers to that woman

explanation.surface: She might produce engravings and much else, that woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who etches cuts designs into metal plates for printing, an engraver.

clue.text: He is Henry's old prot

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
a ward is a young person under a guardian's protection

explanation.surface: Henry's former favourite is named.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR lost the accented ending of 'protégé'. Catherine Howard was a wife of Henry VIII, which colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Howard is a man's first name, so a man, someone referred to as he.

clue.text: Overrule girl's let

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, and the 's adds the S
allow means let, permit

explanation.surface: Someone overrules a girl's permission.
explanation.definitionFit: To disallow is to reject or overturn a claim or decision.

clue.text: Additional support

explanation.surface: Extra backing, put in two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A second helping is an extra one; to second a motion is to back it.

clue.text: One carrying a burning flame to expel the French parliamentarian

parts.note: to blow out is to expel air
la is French for the
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman expels an MP and passes on a torch.
explanation.definitionFit: A plumber's tool that directs a hot jet of flame, also called a blowtorch.

clue.text: River has sediment

parts.note: the Lee is a river in London and Ireland
has is shortened to 's

explanation.surface: A river carries silt.
explanation.definitionFit: Dregs settling at the bottom of wine or beer, the deposit in a bottle.

clue.text: Normal river salmon

parts.note: par is the normal standard

explanation.surface: An ordinary salmon in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A parr is a young salmon before it heads to sea.

clue.text: Chop a savoury cake

explanation.surface: A cook chops something to make a savoury patty.
explanation.definitionFit: A chop or cutlet is a small cut of meat on the bone; a cutlet is also a flat croquette of minced food.

clue.text: Before Lorraine Pascale eventually cooked

indicators.note: eventually picks the letter that comes at the end of the chef's surname
cooked means the letters are prepared afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: TV chef Lorraine Pascale finally gets the dish made.
explanation.walkthrough: Lorraine Pascale is a British television cook; 'cooked' turns LORRAINE plus E into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier on means beforehand, at a previous time.

clue.text: Colour reportedly had faded

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: dyed means coloured, with had giving the past tense

explanation.surface: The paint colour had reportedly worn away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' points to the past tense of colouring with dye.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that died away faded out and came to an end.
